name: AccuTite

lead: AccuTite is a minimally invasive radiofrequency device from InMode that heats tissue under the skin to tighten it and reduce small fat deposits, mainly on the face and neck.
Surgeons present it as an option between noninvasive devices and a facelift. Published evidence is limited to small studies, case series and reviews.

paras: Radiofrequency energy is delivered into the subdermal space to heat dermal collagen and fat. Reviews describe this as targeting skin laxity and adipose tissue together.
Reviews describe lower risk than revision facelifts, but no detailed complication rates for AccuTite appear in the available literature reviewed, and studies are small.

lead: AccuTite is a minimally invasive radiofrequency-assisted lipolysis device from InMode, used for small-area skin tightening and fat reduction, typically on the face and neck. Published reports describe it, together with FaceTite, as delivering radiofrequency energy into the subdermal space to target dermal collagen and excess fat with less downtime and lower cost than open procedures such as neck lifts.[1]

Surgeon-authored papers describe a so-called treatment gap of patients whose laxity is too great for noninvasive devices but not severe enough, or not desired, for a facelift.[2] The evidence consists of small registered studies, case series and review articles.

paras: A 2022 review in facial plastic surgery describes FaceTite and AccuTite as percutaneous devices that deliver energy beneath the skin to heat dermal collagen and fat, positioned as an option for skin laxity and excess fat of the face and neck with less downtime, lower cost and decreased risk of complications compared with more aggressive surgery.[1] AccuTite is the smaller-scale member of the InMode radiofrequency-assisted family, which also includes BodyTite for larger body areas.

Authors describe use for jowl and neck laxity, including recurrence of laxity after a facelift, where radiofrequency-assisted lipolysis has been combined with radiofrequency microneedling as an alternative to revision surgery.[3][4] A 2025 paper presents an anatomical approach to radiofrequency-assisted facial rejuvenation for patients in the treatment gap.[2] A surgeon commentary lists AccuTite among minimally invasive radiofrequency procedures it uses alongside open surgery for body contouring.[5]

A 2021 study evaluated radiofrequency-assisted lipolysis with radiofrequency microneedling for premature jowl and neck laxity following facialplasty;[3] it corresponds to a registered trial of 11 participants.[4] A registered proof-of-concept study of 12 participants evaluated AccuTite with or without Morpheus8 for lower eyelid rejuvenation in periorbital edema.[6] No large randomised trials are listed among the sources reviewed.

Reviewers describe the approach as safe when used by trained surgeons, while contrasting its risks with those of revision facelifts.[1][2] Published case series are small, and no specific complication rates for AccuTite are given in the sources reviewed.
